mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's two tithes from one אתרוג, the two explanations and the challenges to each, and whether an אתרוג's tithing new year is תשרי or ט״ו בשבט
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about רבי עקיבא, who picked an אתרוג on א׳ בשבט and separated two different tithes from it. The first view says he was covering both sides of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל over the date of ראש השנה לאילנות. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says instead that the doubt was between רבן גמליאל, who tithes an אתרוג by when it is picked like a vegetable, and רבי אליעזר, who treats it fully as a tree. The גמרא challenges the first view: we may not take the stringencies of both sides of a dispute. It answers that רבי עקיבא followed בית הלל but was unsure whether their date was א׳ בשבט or ט״ו בשבט. The גמרא then asks why רבי יוסי בר יהודה's story happened on א׳ בשבט, which is בית שמאי's date. רבי חנינא answers that the fruit began growing before the previous ט״ו בשבט, and the date is just when the event happened. רבינא answers instead that the ברייתא should be read as happening on ט״ו בשבט. Finally, רבה בר רב הונא says that for רבן גמליאל an אתרוג's new year is תשרי, and the גמרא challenges him with a ברייתא that divides picked אתרוגים at ט״ו בשבט.

steps.title: One tithe for each school's opinion
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes explaining why רבי עקיבא separated two tithes. One follows בית שמאי and one follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: One tithe was according to the words of בית שמאי, and one tithe was according to the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its story. רבי עקיבא separated two different tithes, one to satisfy each side of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, ראש השנה לאילנות is on the first of שבט, so an אתרוג picked that day already belongs to the new year. That new year was one that requires מעשר עני. For בית הלל, the new year only starts on the fifteenth, so the fruit still belongs to the old year, which requires מעשר שני. Because רבי עקיבא was unsure, he covered both possibilities.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי; here, they hold that the new year for trees is the first of שבט
The school of הלל; here, they hold that the new year for trees is the fifteenth of שבט
According to the words (opinion) of

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new topic. It is the end of a story that began on the previous amud: רבי עקיבא picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט and separated two tithes. This line explains why he separated two.

phrases.english: One [tithe] was according to the words of Beit Shammai,
phrases.notes: For בית שמאי, the new year for trees was already reached on א׳ בשבט, so this tithe was מעשר עני.

phrases.english: and one was according to the words of Beit Hillel.
phrases.notes: For בית הלל, the fruit was still in the old year, so this tithe was מעשר שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְאֶחָד כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's account of רבי עקיבא, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's two tithes were meant to satisfy both בית שמאי's date (first of שבט) and בית הלל's date (fifteenth of שבט) for the new year of trees.

steps.title: A different explanation of the two tithes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says the two tithes were not about בית שמאי and בית הלל. They were about the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: רבי עקיבא was not acting to follow the practice of בית שמאי and בית הלל. He was acting to follow the practice of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with the first explanation of the story. He says the doubt came from a completely different dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts of the story stay the same: two tithes from one אתרוג. Only the reason for the doubt changes. It is no longer about which date starts the year for trees. Instead, it is about how an אתרוג is classified for tithes, which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who offers the alternative explanation
Practice or custom; here, the ruling one acts by
He acted with it (treated the אתרוג this way)
Not this... rather that; a formula that replaces one explanation with another

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ,
phrases.english: He did not act with it according to the practice of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִנְהַג רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נָהַג בָּהּ.
phrases.english: rather, he acted with it according to the practice of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: The source for this dispute is quoted in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation in step 1 with a different reason for the same two tithes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's double tithing reflects doubt between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר, not between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: The source: an אתרוג is like a tree in three ways and like a vegetable in one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה showing that רבן גמליאל treats an אתרוג like a vegetable for tithes. For tithes, what counts is when it is picked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: An אתרוג is like a tree in three ways and like a vegetable in one way. It is like a tree in three ways: for ערלה, for רבעי, and for שביעית. It is like a vegetable in one way: its tithe year is set by the time it is picked. These are the words of רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the dispute that רבי יוסי בר יהודה mentioned. This step gives רבן גמליאל's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, tree fruit is tithed according to the year in which it formed on the tree. Vegetables are tithed according to the year in which they are picked. רבן גמליאל says the אתרוג follows the vegetable rule for tithes only. For ערלה, רבעי and שביעית it remains a regular tree. So for רבן גמליאל, an אתרוג picked in the new year is tithed as new-year produce.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה); introduces a quoted source
Citron
Fruit of a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Fourth-year fruit, which must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
The Sabbatical year
Picking or harvesting; the vegetable standard for tithes

steps.confusionAlert: רבן גמליאל is not saying the אתרוג is a vegetable. It is a tree in its basic category. He only gives it one exceptional rule: its tithe year follows picking, the way a vegetable's does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a single אתרוג could fall into two different tithe years. That is exactly why רבי עקיבא, unsure whose opinion is the הלכה, separated two tithes.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים,
phrases.english: As we learned: An etrog is like a tree in three ways,
and like a vegetable in one way.
It is like a tree in three ways:
for orla, for fourth-year fruit, and for the Sabbatical Year;
and like a vegetable in one way —
that its tithing goes by the time of its picking,
phrases.notes: Its tithe year is set by when it is picked, not by when the fruit formed.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה behind the dispute named in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a real dispute exists between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר about the tithe year of an אתרוג
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (ביכורים ב:ו) quoting רבן גמליאל that an אתרוג is tithed according to its picking

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: an אתרוג is like a tree in every way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that an אתרוג follows tree rules for everything, including tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: An אתרוג is like a tree in every matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing side. רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבן גמליאל and treats the אתרוג fully as a tree, even for tithes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the tithe year of an אתרוג follows the time its fruit formed, as with all tree fruit. So an אתרוג that formed in the old year but was picked in the new year can belong to a different tithe year than it would for רבן גמליאל. רבי עקיבא's two tithes covered both views.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with רבן גמליאל here
In every matter (no exceptions)
Tree

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations for רבי עקיבא's two tithes. (1) The first view: doubt about the date of ראש השנה לאילנות, which is the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. (2) רבי יוסי בר יהודה: doubt about whether an אתרוג is tithed by picking (רבן גמליאל) or by tree rules (רבי אליעזר).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
An etrog is like a tree in every matter.
phrases.notes: This includes tithes, which follow the time the fruit formed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן לְכׇל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same משנה, completing the dispute that רבי יוסי בר יהודה relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, an אתרוג follows tree rules for all matters, including the tithe year.

steps.title: Challenge: May a person take on the stringencies of both sides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא could follow both בית שמאי and בית הלל. A ברייתא says that taking the stringencies of both sides is foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really act according to two stringencies? It was taught in a ברייתא: The הלכה always follows בית הלל. If someone wants to follow בית שמאי, he may. If he wants to follow בית הלל, he may. If he takes the leniencies of both, he is wicked. If he takes the stringencies of both, about him the verse says, 'The fool walks in darkness.' Rather, he should follow either בית שמאי, in both their leniencies and their stringencies, or בית הלל, in both their leniencies and their stringencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first explanation of רבי עקיבא's two tithes. It brings a ברייתא saying that you may not take the stringencies of both opinions at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 1, רבי עקיבא separated one tithe to satisfy בית שמאי and one to satisfy בית הלל. That is exactly 'taking the stringencies of both.' The ברייתא calls such a person a כסיל (fool), so how could רבי עקיבא do it?

keyTerms.meaning: Stringency / stringencies
Leniency / leniencies
But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge from a source)
A wicked person
A fool

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not forbid being careful. It forbids mixing and matching the rulings of two opposing systems. You should choose one side and follow it consistently.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a classic source for the rule that you may not cherry-pick between two disputing opinions, whether to be lenient or to be strict.

phrases.english: But do we act according to two stringencies?
phrases.notes: The challenge is aimed at רבי עקיבא's two tithes.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita:
The halacha is always like the words of Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי — עוֹשֶׂה.
phrases.english: and one who wants to act like Beit Shammai may do so.
One who wants to act like Beit Hillel may do so.

phrases.aramaic: מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית הִלֵּל — רָשָׁע.
phrases.english: One who takes the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the leniencies of Beit Hillel is wicked.

phrases.aramaic: מֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל —
phrases.english: One who takes the stringencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel —
about him the verse says: 'And the fool walks in darkness.'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִי כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי — בְּקוּלֵּיהוֹן וּבְחוּמְרֵיהוֹן.
phrases.english: Rather: either like Beit Shammai, in their leniencies and their stringencies,
or like Beit Hillel, in their leniencies and their stringencies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It returns to the first version of the ברייתא (Step 1) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי עקיבא separated two tithes to satisfy both בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids taking the stringencies of both disputing schools, yet that is what רבי עקיבא appears to have done.

steps.title: Answer: רבי עקיבא was unsure what בית הלל's date was
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא was not mixing opinions. He followed בית הלל, but he was unsure whether their date was א׳ בשבט or ט״ו בשבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא was unsure about what he had learned. He did not know whether בית הלל said א׳ בשבט or ט״ו בשבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי עקיבא's two tithes came from a doubt, not from combining two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא wanted to follow only בית הלל. He was not sure whether his tradition gave בית הלל's date as א׳ בשבט or ט״ו בשבט, so he covered both possibilities. Being strict out of a doubt is allowed. Only choosing the stringencies of two different opinions is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: His tradition, what he had learned from his teachers
He was in doubt
Was said

steps.confusionAlert: In the end, רבי עקיבא only followed בית הלל. The second tithe came from his doubt about בית הלל's own date, not from following בית שמאי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva was in doubt about his tradition,
and he did not know whether Beit Hillel
said it was on the first of Shevat,
or said it was on the fifteenth of Shevat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the motive: the strictness came from a doubt, not from combining two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא took the stringencies of both בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא followed בית הלל alone and was strict only because he was unsure of their date.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יוסי בר יהודה: acting on א׳ בשבט looks like בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version again. It asks why the story took place on א׳ בשבט, since that is בית שמאי's date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: He did not act according to the practice of בית שמאי and בית הלל. He acted according to the practice of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר. But on א׳ בשבט? That means he acted like בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יוסי בר יהודה's words from the ברייתא in order to challenge them. If the story happened on א׳ בשבט, it seems to depend on בית שמאי's date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says the dispute behind the two tithes was רבן גמליאל versus רבי אליעזר, not בית שמאי versus בית הלל. But the date א׳ בשבט only matters to בית שמאי. According to בית הלל, nothing changes until ט״ו בשבט, so there would be no reason to separate two tithes on א׳ בשבט.

keyTerms.meaning: Practice / custom
He acted with it (with the אתרוג)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. The גמרא repeats רבי יוסי בר יהודה's words from Step 2 only to set up a question on them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ,
phrases.english: He did not act with it according to the practice of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִנְהַג רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נָהַג בָּהּ.
phrases.english: but rather he acted with it according to the practice of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט — כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָהַג בָּהּ!
phrases.english: On the first of Shevat? Then he acted like Beit Shammai!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָהַג בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It returns to the second version of the ברייתא (Steps 2–4) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version, which connects the two tithes to the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The date א׳ בשבט only matters according to בית שמאי. So רבי עקיבא would seem to be following בית שמאי, even though the הלכה follows בית הלל.

steps.title: Answer: The fruit began growing before the previous ט״ו בשבט
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains the case. The אתרוג's fruit began to grow before the previous ט״ו בשבט, so the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר applies even according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said, and some say it was רבי חנניא: Here we are dealing with an אתרוג whose fruit began to grow before ט״ו בשבט of the previous year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing the case more precisely. Then the story works even according to בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit began growing (חנטה) before the previous ט״ו בשבט, so it belongs to year 2, which has מעשר שני. It was picked (לקיטה) on the following א׳ בשבט, which falls in year 3, which has מעשר עני. רבי אליעזר goes by when the fruit began growing, so he requires מעשר שני. רבן גמליאל goes by when it was picked, so he requires מעשר עני. That is why רבי עקיבא separated both, all according to בית הלל's date of ט״ו בשבט.

keyTerms.meaning: Began to form (the first growth stage of the fruit)
Of the other one (here, the previous year's)
Here we are dealing with (narrows down the case)
And some say (an alternate name for the speaker)

steps.confusionAlert: The fruit began growing almost a full year before it was picked. So the two moments fall on opposite sides of ט״ו בשבט even by בית הלל's count.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said, and some say it was Rabbi Chananya:
Here we are dealing with an etrog whose fruits began to form

phrases.aramaic: קוֹדֶם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר דְּאִידַּךְ שְׁבָט עָסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: before the fifteenth of the other (previous) Shevat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּאֶתְרוֹג שֶׁחָנְטוּ פֵּירוֹתָיו קוֹדֶם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר דְּאִידַּךְ שְׁבָט עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן): the fruit began growing in the previous year
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story on א׳ בשבט depends on בית שמאי's new year.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the fruit began growing before the previous ט״ו בשבט, the case works according to בית הלל, and only the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר matters.

steps.title: Why א׳ בשבט is mentioned: that is when the story happened
steps.stepSummary: The same would be true even if the fruit had been picked earlier. The ברייתא mentions א׳ בשבט only because that is when the event actually took place.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, the same would apply even earlier. But the event that happened, happened this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It explains why the ברייתא names א׳ בשבט if that date is not really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the fruit began growing before the previous ט״ו בשבט, picking it at any time after that ט״ו בשבט would create the same dispute. The date א׳ בשבט carries no legal weight. It is just a historical detail of the actual story.

keyTerms.meaning: And by right it should be (the law would be the same)
The incident that happened, happened this way

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's two tithes do not involve mixing the stringencies of opposing schools. In the first version, he was unsure of בית הלל's date. In רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version, the fruit began growing before the previous ט״ו בשבט, so the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר applies even according to בית הלל. The date א׳ בשבט is just when the story happened.

phrases.english: And by right, it would be so even earlier than that,
but the incident that happened, happened this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It completes Step 8's answer by explaining why the ברייתא mentions א׳ בשבט.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining a detail in the text as historical, not legal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The date א׳ בשבט must be legally important.
steps.terutzMaskana: The date is mentioned only because that is when the event happened. The law would be the same if the fruit had been picked earlier.

steps.title: רבינא rereads the story as happening on ט״ו בשבט
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers differently from רבי חנינא. He says we should read the ברייתא as if the story happened on ט״ו בשבט. On that reading, רבי עקיבא gave double tithes because of the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Join the two statements together and read the ברייתא this way. It was not on א׳ בשבט, it was on ט״ו בשבט. And רבי עקיבא was not following the practices of בית שמאי and בית הלל. He was following the practices of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second answer to the problem from Step 7. He changes how we read the story: the date was ט״ו בשבט, and the two opinions רבי עקיבא worried about were רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא kept the date as א׳ בשבט and explained it with a special case where the fruit started growing early. רבינא instead says the ברייתא should be read with the date ט״ו בשבט. On that day, רבן גמליאל (who goes by picking, like a vegetable) and רבי אליעזר (who treats it like a tree) reach different results, so רבי עקיבא tithed both ways. Because the story now happens on בית הלל's date, it no longer looks like he was following בית שמאי, which was the problem raised in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Combine and teach: read the two parts of the text together as one corrected version
Practice or custom: here, the ruling or opinion that someone follows
He acted with it: he treated the fruit according to that practice
The תנא who treats an אתרוג like a tree for tithing, against רבן גמליאל

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא's reading does not bring בית שמאי back into the story. With the date set at ט״ו בשבט, the case fits בית הלל's new year. The only doubt left is the separate dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר over how an אתרוג is tithed.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא solves Step 7's problem by changing the date in the ברייתא, while רבי חנינא kept the date and narrowed the case instead. The גמרא records both answers without choosing between them.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Combine and teach:
It was not on the first of Shevat
but it was on the fifteenth of Shevat,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ —
phrases.english: and he did not act with it by the practice of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel,
phrases.notes: He was not worried about the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute over the date.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִנְהַג רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נָהַג בָּהּ.
phrases.english: but he acted with it by the practice of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: He tithed in a way that satisfied both opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question in Step 7, instead of רבי חנינא's answer in Steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text (changing the date and the dispute being followed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version, the story happened on א׳ בשבט, which seems to make it depend on בית שמאי's date.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story happened on ט״ו בשבט, and רבי עקיבא was being careful about the dispute between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר, all within בית הלל.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: the אתרוג's new year is תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says that since רבן גמליאל treats an אתרוג like a vegetable for tithing, its new year must be תשרי, just like vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Now that רבן גמליאל has said that an אתרוג is tithed by the time it is picked, like a vegetable, its new year is תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion starts here. רבה בר רב הונא takes רבן גמליאל's rule to its logical end: if an אתרוג is like a vegetable, it should also have a vegetable's new year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vegetables follow the picking date, and their tithing year changes on א׳ תשרי. רבה בר רב הונא says רבן גמליאל's comparison goes all the way. So the cutoff for an אתרוג would be תשרי and not ט״ו בשבט.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that he said: introduces what follows from an earlier statement
Picking or harvesting of the fruit
Tithing: deciding which year's tithes apply
Vegetable: tithed by when it is picked
The month whose first day is the new year for vegetables

steps.whyThisMatters: If this is right, then according to רבן גמליאל, ט״ו בשבט would have nothing to do with an אתרוג. The next step tests that claim.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Now that Rabban Gamliel has said
that an etrog's tithing follows its picking, like a vegetable,
its new year is Tishrei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion. It builds on רבן גמליאל's opinion from the משנה in Step 3 and draws a new conclusion about when an אתרוג's new year falls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן גמליאל, the tithing new year of an אתרוג is א׳ תשרי, like vegetables.

steps.title: A ברייתא uses ט״ו בשבט as the dividing line for picked אתרוגים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר רב הונא with a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר goes by the picking date, like רבן גמליאל, yet he treats ט״ו בשבט as the dividing line between years. That suggests the new year is not תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: If someone picked אתרוגים on the eve of ט״ו בשבט before sunset, and then picked more after sunset, he may not separate תרומה and מעשרות from one batch for the other. This is because we do not separate from new produce for old, or from old produce for new. If it was the third year of the cycle going into the fourth: from the third-year fruit he gives מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני, and from the fourth-year fruit he gives מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר רב הונא. A ברייתא divides אתרוגים by picking time, and it puts the line at sunset going into ט״ו בשבט, not at תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר judges the fruit by when it was picked, which is רבן גמליאל's approach. Even so, he sets the change of year at ט״ו בשבט, so fruit picked minutes apart belongs to different years. This goes directly against רבה בר רב הונא's claim that the year of a picked אתרוג changes at תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection: a challenge from a תנאי source
The eve: the day before, which becomes the next date at sunset
Separating תרומה and tithes
New crop and old crop (from different tithing years)
Tithe for the poor, given in years 3 and 6 of the שמיטה cycle
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים, given in years 1, 2, 4, and 5

steps.confusionAlert: 'ערב ט״ו בשבט' means the 14th of שבט. Fruit picked before sunset belongs to the old year. Fruit picked after sunset is already on the 15th and belongs to the new year. That is why the two batches cannot be tithed for each other.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: לִיקֵּט אֶתְרוֹג עֶרֶב חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בִּשְׁבָט
phrases.english: If one picked an etrog on the eve of the fifteenth of Shevat
before the sun set,
and then picked again after the sun set,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין וּמְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: one may not separate teruma and tithes from this for that,
because one does not separate teruma and tithes
neither from the new for the old
nor from the old for the new.
If it was the third year going into the fourth,
phrases.notes: The years of the seven-year שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: the third-year fruit gives first tithe and poor man's tithe,
the fourth-year fruit gives first tithe and second tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבה בר רב הונא's claim in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's claim that, according to רבן גמליאל, the new year of a picked אתרוג is תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר divides אתרוגים by when they were picked, as רבן גמליאל does. Yet he treats ט״ו בשבט as the change of year. So even when we go by picking, the new year for an אתרוג seems to be ט״ו בשבט and not תשרי.
